stories.title: Types, manifest scope, store paths and the scope-aware registry view
stories.description: Add InstallScope = "repo" | "user", ArcaneManifest.scope? and fanout?, and user? on the init/update options in src/types.ts; validate scope in src/modules/manifest.ts like the other enums; create src/modules/user-tier.ts with userTierRoot() (homedir resolved on every call), USER_TIER_COMPONENTS (= SPELL_COMPONENT_NAMES), componentForScope(component, scope) (user: canonical files only, installed path spells/<id>.md, asset mapped via sourceOverrides) and toAbsoluteSpellPath(root, id) with forward slashes (architecture D1, D2).
acceptanceCriteria: readManifest rejects scope values other than repo/user with ManifestInvalidFieldError and accepts a manifest with no scope
componentForScope(c, "repo") returns c unchanged; componentForScope(c, "user") lists exactly one file per spell (spells/<id>.md) with sourceOverrides mapping each to .arcane/spells/<id>.md
userTierRoot() changes when USERPROFILE/HOME change between calls
npm run typecheck passes

stories.title: Fan-out engine with the ARC-038 hash discipline outside the store
stories.description: In src/modules/user-tier.ts implement syncUserTierFanout({ homeDir, storeRoot, spellIds, previous, dryRun }) producing the desired set (~/.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md via renderCodexSkill and ~/.claude/commands/<id>.md via renderClaudeCommandStub, both with the absolute forward-slash canonical path) and reconciling it against the recorded fanout map: write/record, rewrite-on-change, keep-customized (hash carried forward), collision (never recorded), prune only when hash-matched plus emptied-directory removal, dry-run parity. renderClaudeCommandStub gains an optional canonicalRef parameter defaulting to canonicalSpellPath(id) (architecture D3).
acceptanceCriteria: First run on an empty temp home writes 2 files per spell and returns a record with one hash per file; a second run writes nothing and reports every file unchanged
An edited fan-out file is left byte-identical, reported as customized, and its previously recorded hash is carried forward
A same-named file that was never recorded is left untouched, reported as a collision, and absent from the returned record
A spell removed from the desired set has its recorded, hash-matched files deleted and its emptied <id> directory removed; an edited one is kept and reported
dryRun writes nothing to disk and reports the same decisions
Rendered content contains the absolute canonical path with forward slashes and never a repo-relative .arcane/spells path

stories.title: spell init --user and the CLI wiring
stories.description: Add --user to init/update/status/uninstall in src/index.ts (targetDir = userTierRoot(), options carry user: true). In src/commands/init.ts a user-scope path installs USER_TIER_COMPONENTS through componentForScope into the store, writes the manifest with scope: "user" and fanout, runs the fan-out and prints the store path, counts, the VS Code note and next steps — with no profile prompt, no git checks, no manifest questions, no hooks, no agent setup; --dry-run and --force honored (architecture D4, D5, D6).
acceptanceCriteria: runInit({ user: true, profile: undefined }, ...) on a stubbed home creates ~/.arcane/.arcane.json with scope user, 41 files under ~/.arcane/spells/, 41 files under ~/.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md and 41 under ~/.claude/commands/, and a fanout record of 82 entries
No @inquirer/prompts function and no git module function is called during a --user init
--dry-run writes nothing and prints the would-copy/would-write lines; a second init reports Already initialized
The printed output contains the VS Code note naming chat.useAgentSkills and stating that chat.promptFilesLocations is not used
spell --help shows --user on init, update, status and uninstall

stories.title: spell update --user: store update through the scope view, then fan-out regeneration
stories.description: In src/commands/update.ts: for scope user skip the git checks and the commit-first warning, resolve registry components through componentForScope, fetch the previously published vendor file by its asset path (sourceOverrides[file] ?? file — the general fix), skip retrofits, and after the store update reconcile the fan-out (regenerating changed shims, pruning dropped spells) and persist the new fanout record; --dry-run and --prune as for a repo (architecture D2, D4).
acceptanceCriteria: A deleted ~/.arcane/spells/<id>.md is restored by a same-version spell update --user and its missing fan-out files are rewritten
An edited store spell goes through the three-way merge with the network mocked, and the fetch is requested at the asset path .arcane/spells/<id>.md
A --user update never calls inspectGitRepository and never asks a retrofit question
--dry-run reports the store and fan-out decisions without writing
Existing repo-tier update tests pass unchanged

stories.title: spell status --user and spell uninstall --user
stories.description: status: for the store print the component table, Scope: user, one fan-out line with per-client counts plus customized/missing counts, then the version footer; plain repo status prints Scope: repo and, only when a store exists, a User tier line. uninstall: reconcile the fan-out against an empty set (hash-checked, customized kept and listed), remove store files and the manifest, skip the push-policy refusal and repository-only cleanups; --yes and --dry-run honored (architecture D4).
acceptanceCriteria: status --user output contains Scope: user and the fan-out counts; a customized fan-out file is counted as customized and a deleted one as missing
Plain status prints Scope: repo, and the User tier line appears only when ~/.arcane/.arcane.json exists in the stubbed home
uninstall --user removes every hash-matched fan-out file, its emptied <id> directories, the store files and the manifest; an edited fan-out file is kept and named in the output
uninstall --user --dry-run lists what would be removed and deletes nothing; no push-safety or marker-section code runs for scope user

stories.title: spell doctor: non-blocking user-tier check
stories.description: Add checkUserTier() to src/commands/doctor.ts and the runDoctor check list: no store → pass with the optional-install message; store present → warn when the store's major.minor differs from the CLI's, and warn when the recorded fan-out has missing or edited files, each with the spell update --user remedy; never blocking, never reading VS Code settings (architecture D4).
acceptanceCriteria: With no store in the stubbed home the check passes and names spell init --user
A store at a different major.minor produces a warn row (blocking false) naming spell update --user
A missing or edited recorded fan-out file produces a warn row with counts; doctor's exit code is unaffected
Existing doctor tests pass unchanged
